key_insight: A hybrid quantum-classical ensemble with QSVM and VQC improves phishing detection in Ethereum transaction networks, with QSVM showing the strongest recall and lowest false negatives.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests QML can be a practical anomaly-detection tool for blockchain security, especially when combined with classical models and robust feature encodings.
method: Compared QSVM and VQC on real Ethereum transaction data.
Tested cascaded Quantum Random Access Coding (QRAC) against the ZZ feature map.
Evaluated performance on simulators and the IBM Heron quantum processor.
evidence_signal: QRAC improved performance over ZZ by 13% for VQC and 3% for QSVM, and QSVM consistently achieved the lowest false negatives and higher recall.
watch_item: Current QML gains still do not fully match cutting-edge deep learning methods, and hardware constraints can affect reproducibility on real quantum devices.
paper_title: Detecting Phishing in Ethereum Networks using Quantum Machine Learning
